company.name: Milky Mist Dairy Food
company.summary: Milky Mist buys milk from farmers and turns it into paneer, cheese, curd, ice cream, yogurt and other dairy products sold across India.
company.description: Milk spoils within days, so a dairy company must collect it, cool it and process it quickly. Milky Mist collects milk from farmers and dairy operators, cools it at chilling centres, and makes it into products with a longer shelf life and a higher price: paneer (a fresh Indian cheese), cheese, curd, ice cream, yogurt, ghee and butter. It makes most of them at a large, highly automated plant in Perundurai in Tamil Nadu, and moves them in its own vehicles to distributors, who supply shops across India. Its shares began trading on the exchanges in August 2026.
company.ownership: This profile covers Milky Mist Dairy Food Limited, based in Perundurai, Erode district, Tamil Nadu, and its subsidiary Asal Food Products Private Limited. It buys milk and makes dairy products; it does not own the shops that sell them. Its shares began trading on the exchanges in August 2026, so it has reported only a few quarters as a listed company.
products: Made from milk, with whey left over
Thicker yogurts the company sells as high-protein
Milk from farmers and chilling centres
company.money: Milky Mist earns money when distributors and shops pay for its products. Its largest cost is raw milk, which it buys from farmers and other dairy operators and whose price changes with seasons and farm conditions. It also pays for sugar, packaging, cultures and other ingredients, factory work, transport, advertising, and the fridges and freezers it places in shops. A rise in milk prices cuts what is left from each sale unless the company can raise its own prices.
watch: Is the cost of milk rising faster than the prices Milky Mist can charge?
Milk is the biggest cost and farm prices change with the seasons and weather.
Which products are driving growth, and for how long?
A category growing fast from a small base can look better than it is.
How dependable is the milk supply?
The company’s own documents say most farmers have no formal agreement with it.
Is the expanded plant being used?
Extra capacity adds costs whether or not it is full.
How much cash is tied up in coolers, stock and unpaid bills?
Growth that needs a lot of cash can strain a company even when profit is rising.
risks: Milk costs rise or supply falls
Farmers are not obliged to sell to Milky Mist, so a shortage or a price spike can reduce output or squeeze margins.
Dairy is perishable. A fridge breakdown, a delayed truck or a power cut can spoil stock and harm the brand.
Large cooperative and private dairy brands compete for the same shelf space and customers, which can limit pricing.
The offer document discloses two notices dated 31 December 2024 from the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board about water and air rules. Compliance problems can lead to extra costs or restrictions.
Expansion goes over budget or runs late
The plant expansion depends on outside contractors and equipment suppliers, and the offer document says costs and timing may change.
sources: NSE circular announcing the listing · 17 August 2026
update: October 2026: costs rose across dairy, yet profit grew faster than sales

Milky Mist’s investor presentation of 29 October 2026 covers the quarter to September 2026. Management says the dairy industry faced higher input costs and cautious consumers, and that the company still reported higher sales, better margins and much faster profit growth. It credits price increases, higher use of its plant, a wide range of products and efficiency gains. Yogurt was its fastest-growing category. These are the company’s own explanations, from its early quarterly reports as a listed company. Compare them with the full-year figures at the end of this page, which cover an earlier period.
company.question: When a company sells new shares in an IPO and its existing owners also sell shares, does all the money go to the company?
company.answer: No. Money from newly issued shares goes to the company. Money from shares sold by existing owners goes to those owners. Check which part is which to see how much the business receives.
